import base64, itertools, string
base="ZmxhZ3swhjNidDFIM1ISQOGOhiQ=="
alts={'w':'wvW','O':'O0QG','G':'G6C','h':'hbn','j':'jin','Q':'Q0O','I':'I1l','R':'R8B','1':'1l7I','0':'0OoQ','D':'DO0','8':'8B','h':'hn','$':'$']':'}
pos=[i for i,c in enumerate(base) if c in alts]
cands=set()
opts=[alts.get(base[i],base[i]) for i in range(len(base))]
import itertools
# limit combinations
cnt=0
for combo in itertools.product(*[opts[i] for i in range(len(base))]):
    s=''.join(combo)
    if len(s)%4: continue
    try: d=base64.b64decode(s,validate=True)
    except Exception: continue
    if all(32<=c<127 for c in d) and d.startswith(b'flag{') and d.endswith(b'}'):
        cands.add(d); 
    cnt+=1
    if cnt>2000000: break
print(len(cands)); print(list(cands)[:20])

Brute-force plausible base64 confusions (w/o, O/0, Q/0, I/l, 1/l, etc.) and keep decodings that are printable flag-shaped.
The decoded output is still garbled, so OCR is misreading some base64 characters. I'll brute-force the ambiguous characters and keep only candidates that decode to printable text ending in `}`.

from PIL import Image, ImageFilter
import numpy as np, pytesseract
A=np.array(Image.open('/workspace/image1.png').convert('1'))
B=np.array(Image.open('/workspace/image2.png').convert('1'))
X=(A^B)
base=Image.fromarray((X*255).astype(np.uint8))
for sc in (2,3,4,6):
    im=base.resize((256*sc,256*sc),Image.LANCZOS).filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(1))
    im=im.point(lambda p:255 if p>128 else 0)
    for psm in (4,6):
        t=pytesseract.image_to_string(im,config=f'--psm {psm} -c tessedit_char_whitelist=ZmxhgFIMOQ0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ+/=')
        print(sc,psm,repr(t.strip()))
